title_options: Agent Memory Filters: Why Top-k Returns Too Few Results
Scoped Memory Retrieval: Put the Tenant Filter Before the Ranking
Post-Filtered Top-k in Agent Memory: The Rows That Never Come Back
presentation.title_rationale: The reader problem is a caller asking for five memories and receiving one or two because the tenant filter runs after a global ranking. The selected title frontloads the product topic (agent memory filters) and states the one supported outcome (top-k returns too few results) in 55 characters. It avoids the 118-character working headline's subordinate clause and year, drops the 'ships the rest to the model' claim from the headline (that path is one of two failure modes the body measures), and makes no vendor, production or percentage promise. The measured magnitude stays in the description and introduction.
presentation.visual_purpose: A three-stage checklist - tenant filter, candidate ranking, returned top-k - that names the two positions where a filter can sit. The footer reads 'conceptual checklist, not new measurement data', so the image explains the mechanism and scope rather than asserting a measured gain; every number the article reports stays in the body and in summary.json.

proposed_process_improvements: Record for later reviewed maintenance: presentation-only revisions could reuse the approved claim mapping automatically when the body hash is unchanged, instead of asking the Writer to restate it, which risks accidental drift between the receipt and the reviewed text.
